meta.title: Which Trip Shall We Take?
meta.textType: story: a club talk that compares two places

paragraphs: On Thursday, December third, the Explorers met in the school library. It was the club hour after lunch. Teacher Kim, Lily, Mia, Leo, and May sat around a long table. Two posters hung on the wall, and two dates stood on the whiteboard. One poster showed a big blue whale, and the other showed a steaming pot. "We can visit two places in December," said Teacher Kim. "The science museum is on the first date, and Chef Lucy's cooking class is on the second." "Which place shall we visit first?" she asked.

Lily looked at the posters and read the prices. "A ticket for the museum is cheap," she said. "It costs thirty baht." "The cooking class costs eighty baht, so it is quite expensive." "The museum is bigger, but the cooking class is not as far." "First of all, I like machines," said Leo. "The museum has all kinds of machines, and the cooking class does not."

May thought about it for a moment. "I suppose that the museum is more interesting," she said. "The bus is our transport, and it goes to both places." Mia put up her hand. "Are we walking from the bus stop?" she asked. "Yes, for ten minutes," said Teacher Kim. "Walking is fine, and I can look at the street," said Mia. "In the future, I want to build a machine," she added. "Every trip is a small adventure," said Teacher Kim.

"Please raise your hand for the museum," said Teacher Kim. Four hands went up at once. Leo raised his hand high and grinned. Teacher Kim counted with a finger: one, two, three, four. Nobody raised a hand for the cooking class. Lily wrote the result on the whiteboard.

"Then we are visiting the museum on the first date," said Teacher Kim. "We are going to the cooking class a week later." "Lily, are you calling the museum tomorrow?" she asked. "Yes, I am calling at four o'clock," said Lily. "The museum has a whale!" said Leo. Everybody laughed, and the club hour ended.
